utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We move into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon, Ms. Radic. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Ms. Radic. Before, Ms. Friedman, you start your examination-in-chief, the Chamber is informed that a new version of the expert report is submitted where most of pages -- or at least part of page 31 and 45 are stricken and all the pages in between. The Chamber understands this to be that where the major problem may have been in the unsourced description of military historical events, that of course by choosing this way out, that everything that is maybe related to that, that is observations about population movement is then out as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But for the extent to which it appears in other parts of the report and as lay laid out in the various tables next to the report which still documents movement of people, but the description as you described in that section we will not be relying upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear that resolves at least a huge problem the Chamber had with this report, that it gives a totally unsourced description of all kind of facts with all kind of details where one could wonder how, where those facts are taken from, and what in the expertise of this witness would allow her to form an opinion about that where she apparently not has observed it herself. May I take it that this is the result of communication between Defence and Prosecution this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any remaining problems because -- or is this -- could we start not to say that you would agree with everything that remains, Mr. Petrovic or Mr. Jordash, but as a starting point can we proceed on the basis of the expert report as it is submitted now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a brief observation to make. Part 13, which is less than a page has to do with the population fleeing Vojvodina and Serbia, I don't think it is of any relevance to this case and I see no reason for that part to be left in the report. It's not a matter discussed in the indictment and although it's a small part, that should be left out of the report in order to speed things up even further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider or not whether to accept that part. In addition to that, Ms. Friedman, if I look at the fourth paragraph of chapter 13, then I see that still some of methods of expulsion were similar to those already described in Croatia from individual threats and incidents in places with Croatian population to the murders of Croats in the period 1991, 1995, which is similar to what we find in many of the stricken pages. But we'll consider that further, Mr. Petrovic. Ms. Radic, you may have understood that there has been some discussion as to the sources of the knowledge of parts of your report which seem not to be directly linked to your field of expertise, which has resulted in taking out major parts of the report, especially those parts where you describe in some details matters where it's totally unclear from the report what the sources of your knowledge are and which apparently are not directly linked to your field of expertise however, to describe that because, although you are a trained sociologist as I do understand, it has some -- the way in which you worked made you half demographer as well, if I may say it in that way, but much of that information falls outside of the scope both of the direct expert skills of a sociologist or a demographer. Ms. Friedman, are you ready to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first now be examined by Ms. Friedman. Ms. Friedman is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Radic, could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Anna Maria Radic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And have you brought any papers with you to court today which you may wish to refer to during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And did you prepare these paper and notes yourself in preparation for the testimony today, or did you gather them yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the Chamber's leave I would ask that Ms. Radic be permitted to consult these reports and notes if necessary during her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, may before Your Honours rule on this, we clarify exactly what these notes are. My learned friend asked the question whether the witness had prepared the notes for the testimony or gathered them for the testimony, and the two may well be quite different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I suggest the following: Whenever you consider it necessary to consult your notes, we'd like you to inform us about it and also what the notes are about so that we would know that not in general and not spend a lot of time on that, but on each specific occasion where apparently there's a need to go back to your notes, that we -- that you inform us about this and that we know what these notes are, because, Mr. Jordash, it may be far clearer in many circumstances to know what the question is and then sometimes it will be self-explanatory that you would need notes, for example, if you ask about numbers, you would not have learned it by heart and then the notes will be about the numbers. Whereas in other circumstances it may need a totally different clarification. Yes? So please inform us whenever you want to consult your notes, Ms. Radic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, is your current position as the head of the department for areas of special state concern in the ministry of regional development, forestry and water management?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And is it true that this department was formerly called the administration for the return of displaced persons and refugees and that this former entity was the legal successor of the office for displaced person and refugees?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And it was also called administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman, the follow-up of the several institutions, I think I've read it eight, nine, or ten times in the report, so it's really repetitious to what is written down already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And the Office of Displaced Persons and Refugees, was it called the ODPR?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: So when did you begin working for the ODPR?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: From the very beginning in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And does that mean that notwithstanding all the change, that's the office, the ODPR, that you've been working at since 1994?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Not at the same position, but it was with the administration throughout, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And could I ask the Court Officer to please call up 65 ter 5364, the curriculum vitae of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, do you recognise this as a true and accurate copy of your CV?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, my current position is wrong. Head of administration for areas of special state concern and not for areas outside of the areas of special state concern. So I am head of administration for the areas of special state concern, that is the correct title.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And I would ask that this exhibit, 65 ter 5364, be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objections? Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P549, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P549 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask briefly about your first position in the ODPR as spokesperson and public relations officer between 1994 and 2000, and did this position involve preparing any reports?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did. That is why I was employed by the then Office for Displaced Persons and Refugees. I worked in public relations, which included preparing public reports and other types of reports pertaining to displaced persons and refugees who were either accommodated or taken in by Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And did you ever write reports in conjunction with other organisations?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, with governmental organisations, NGOs, and some international organisations such as the UNHCR. We had very close co-operation with them for three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And in your various positions until today, have you had occasion to use the database of displaced persons, refugees, and returnees that you discuss in your report?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And how long have you been working with this database?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Ever since it came into being, and in the forum as it stands today, that was since 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer now call up Ms. Radic's expert report which is 65 ter 5363. Sorry, 5 -- yes, 5363.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: While it's being loaded in the B/C/S, can you say, Ms. Radic, whether you recognise this as your report?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I will continue presuming that it will come on the screen shortly. Now, in your report you've described the registration process of displaced persons and refugees in great detail. So would it be fair to characterise it as beginning as an ad hoc process as soon as the first displaced people began arriving in 1991 into new areas and then involving four separate registrations which were conducted by the ODPR?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: At page 11 in the B/C/S and 16 to 17 in the English, you describe the four official registrations as a registration of displaced persons in April 1992; a registration in March 1993 of refugees from Bosnia-Herzegovina; a third registration in June 2004 of both category, displaced persons and refugees; and a fourth in 1997 which included displaced persons, refugees, and returnees; is that a fair characterisation?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, again, all of this information is contained in your report, so I will just ask you for some specific clarifications. The first thing I would like to ask is whether when you use the term "expelled persons" in your report and then when it appears in the tables, if this is a reference to people who were displaced internally within the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And I now want to ask you just a few questions about the Office of the UN High Commission for Refugees, the UNHCR in Croatia. In your report at page 2 in the English and the B/C/S, you mention that the UNHCR office in Croatia was opened in December 1991, at the same time as the Office for Expelled Persons and refugees, the ODPR, and that the two offices were located in the same premises. My question is whether the UNHCR was involved at all in the work of the ODPR?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the beginning. Our co-operation existed since the very beginning of the process. Naturally, in Croatia there was no expertise, no expert knowledge required to take in and accommodate any displaced persons. We did have a number of organisations which took part, but, for example, in terms of registering IDPs, this type of expert knowledge was key and it came precisely from the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Did they provide any -- you talk about their expert knowledge, was it about the registration process?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, the registration process, but one also needs to keep in mind that they assisted directly in terms of providing humanitarian assistance arriving in Croatia at the time, given that a large segment of the Croatian population had fled their homes. It took a lot of organisation and knowledge and the UNHCR was of great assistance. It all took place, of course, in very close co-operation with our office at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Did they also provide any recommendations as to what to put in the forms that you were using to register people?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And was their advice implemented in subsequent versions of the form?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, section 10 of your report discusses preliminary data from 1991 up until the time of the first formal registration in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Would the Court Usher please display page 17 in B/C/S and 26 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, I'm looking at the second paragraph in English, and it says that the date, in relation to the first records of expulsions record the date as the 1st August of 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Of 1991, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: This must have been a typographical error.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: So I wanted to note that typographical error for the record and also that it appears on page 34 in the English, the second paragraph and page 22 in the B/C/S, the fourth full paragraph as well. I would now like to look at table 1, which is at pages 31 to 32 in B/C/S, and 48 to 49 in English. And I would ask the Court Officer to please pull up those pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: This is an analysis of the population based on the 1991 census. And Ms. Radic, are the municipalities that are named here, the municipalities as they existed at the time in 1991 or as they exist today?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: These municipalities represent the municipalities as they exist today as well as the counties.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. And what does it mean when certain municipalities are highlighted in yellow?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: The municipalities in yellow were those which were not completely out of reach of Croatian authorities. They were only partially occupied in the period between 1991 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And would the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 5368.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, could you tell us, Ms. Radic, what is the difference between group 1 and group 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we have all the areas affected by war in 1991. As of 1996, we refer to them as areas of special state concern when the law on areas of special state concern was passed. It encompassed all of the areas affected by the war and divided into two groups. The first group were those settlements or those areas which had municipal seats which were not further than 15 kilometres from the state border and having less than 5.000 population, including all of the areas of the Croatian Danubian regions; the second group includes all other towns, settlements, and municipalities which between 1991 and 1995 were occupied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, and we will return to the report later so I will tender it later, but for now I would like to call up 5368.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, were you asked to prepare a table which reflects, to the extent that you are able to determine, which municipality in 1991 and which current municipality and county certain places are found in?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And is this the table you prepared?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And the document contains mostly place names, but the headings are in English. Do you understand the English language?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Have you reviewed the table before you?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And is it your signature on the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would now like to look at, well, for example, the first place name and there's -- it says Dubica. And in brackets, it says Hrvatska Dubica, what do these parentheses indicate?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I presume that this is Hrvatska Dubica and not Dubica because such a place does not exist in Croatia without the adjective Hrvatska and its mentioned in a group of other places in the area of Banovina, and because of that I presume that's Hrvatska Dubica.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: When you say "mentioned" are you referring to a mention in the Prosecution's indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And some of the rows have been left blank, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Out of those names listed here, I could not determine which places they referred to. For instance, Cerovljani, there are several places named Cerovljani. They also have a prefix, and addendum. I could not determine such a short time which place this would refer to. However, in our database, there are many settlements, all the settlements in the Republic of Croatia. For instance, the place name Daljska Atar. I could not determine whether it's a geographical toponym or a place name or a name of a settlement. Vukovic as well, it could be a hamlet, part of a bigger village and not a separate entity.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. So for the place names that you were able to indicate the former municipality and current municipality, the information on this table is correct to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this table was prepared to assist the Chamber in cross-referencing the municipalities in the charts that have been provided with the locations in the indictment. And also on the second page of the table, we've included the locations that are mentioned in the relevant adjudicated facts. I've provided copy of these tables to the Defence yesterday and I tender them at this time as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P550 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: In the annexes to your report, tables 2, 3, and 4 all discuss data collected in March 1992 before the official registrations began. Table 3, for example, provides statistics on displaced persons and refugees from the 20th of March, 1992, and it contains five separate tables. Now, table 4 is a similar report, it contains the same types of tables and it is from just one week later, March 27th, 1992. So my question to you, Ms. Radic, is if you can explain why you've included both of these tables in your report?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Those are the original tables dating from the relevant time, I don't have them before me so that I could check. But they differ in one thing, one table is organised by the area where people were accommodated, the other areas in Croatia where they fled to. The second table was, I think, organised by the place of origin of those displaced persons. I do believe that this is the main difference between the tables but that's what I presume because I don't have them before me so that I could verify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- do you actually have a hard copy before you which would assist, and if not we'll call it up on the screen. Do you have the tables to your report?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I don't think that I've got those tables here. If you could please show them on the screen so I can tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 33 in the B/C/S and 50 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And while that's loading, and just to clarify, you are right that there are separate tables based on the municipality of origin and the place of accommodation. We are looking at 65 ter 5363. And both reports from the 20th of March, 1992 and the 27th of March, 1992, have these different tables within them, tables that are based on the regional centre where the refugees registered and tables that are based on their place of origin, but there are two separate reports, one from the 20th of March and one from the 27th of March, and can you clarify why both are included and if there is any difference?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I think the difference that I explained just a while ago is the only difference. I am afraid that this is too small for me to see anything. The number of displaced persons. If you could please zoom in both pages, if possible, please. The table from the 20th of March is organised by the place of accommodation of those displaced persons in Croatia, and it was generated by collecting data from social welfare centres where those people were registered. So this would be one table dated the 20th of March. It contains data on persons registered in Croatia and contains data on persons who are accommodated in other countries in accordance with reports that we used to receive from either the UNHCR or from those third countries.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And so this is table 2, and table 3 relates to the 20th of March as well. Table 4 is from the 27th of March. And how did your office obtain the information from the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: In the same manner. Displaced persons were registered when they arrived at the local social welfare centre. The ODPR had just been established and had not still established a network of field officers so what was used was the present network of social welfare centres. There was one in each municipality in Croatia. And they registered the people when they arrived and sent their reports, which they prepared on a weekly basis, to the office in Zagreb. In the meantime, regional offices for displaced persons and refugees had started being established with welfare centres, and they started to collate individual reports that they received from welfare offices and consolidated them and sent them to the ODPR in Zagreb which then manually collated them and keyed them into touch tables and reports as you see.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question: One of the things that I missed in your report is a copy of the registration form. It's quite common doing this kind of registration that you add a copy of what was registered because we find some of it in the report, but is there any copy available of that registration form so that we know what was asked from those who reported themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I do have on my person forms for registration from -- dating from 1991 and instructions how to fill in the form and samples of the forms used in 1994 and 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Friedman, I would suggest that copies are made from those forms because we are now looking at the results of the registration, but we do not know exactly what was asked and what was not asked. And I'm specifically also paying attention to this because as you may have noticed, there was some concern about what comes from where. For example, if sometimes certain language is used, one wonders whether any questions were put to those who registered in relation to what is assumed or established to be the case. So therefore, I would suggest that during the first break you provide the forms and the instructions and that they will be copied, you'll get back the originals, so that the parties know what exactly you registered and what you asked from those persons who were registering. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can inform you that pursuant to a request from the Defence, we did ask Ms. Radic to provide some forms and she has provided several to us. It was still not something I was going to tender in my examination-in-chief but it's been provided to the Defence and we have it in e-court. We can return to it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am a bit surprised that you left it to the Defence because this is the kind of basic information you need to interpret the outcome. So therefore, I think it would have assisted the Chamber if you would not have waited for the Defence to bring it up, but to inform the Chamber as completely as possible. But we'll see those forms after the break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, I have a few clarifications about the information contained in your database. What is the earliest information that's contained there?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: The data that we have today in the database dates from 1994, as I've already explained. The data in the first statistics reports were collated manually. They were not based on the forms that were later to be used in registration. In 1992 in April, the first registration of displaced persons was made, but the problem with the data was at the time not all data could be introduced into a single database. And quite a lot of data was missing. For that reason, new registration was done in 1994 and from that point onwards, those data are used as data on displaced persons and refugees by being updated daily. So persons registering or taken out of the database, changes in their personal statistics, changes in place of accommodation or type of accommodation, any changes that may affect that population are updated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: So since the information begins in 1994, does that mean that all the data from people who had left their homes in 1991 but had returned before 1994 is not included in the database?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is not to be found in that database.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And other than tables 1 through 5, which contain statistical data from before the 1994 registration, was the database we are discussing the one that was used to prepare the remainder of the tables?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I am afraid you'll have to repeat which table is the same. I did not quite get the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The tables that are from 1992 were obviously not prepared from your database, and my question was whether the rest of the tables which you've included in your report were prepared based on this database?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. All the other tables are derived from the database, apart from the first one which is based on the population census.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: So those tables do not include people who had returned home before 1994?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would now like to discuss tables 7 and 8 in your report.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And if we could turn to table 7 which is at page 49 of the B/C/S and 75 of the English. It would be sufficient, I think, to show it in one language as the important information is either numerical or place names.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, these tables set out the numbers of displaced persons per municipality, but they provide different dates to show the numbers of displaced persons as of certain time periods.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, let me just check the correct page number. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And table 8 is simply an expanded version of this table; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: That's correct. It contains individual municipalities and towns listed therein, whereas this table is organised in counties, so everything is broken down at the level of county.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And we can see how the different dates are set out and show different waves of registration. Ms. Radic, when was this table prepared?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: This table was prepared later on in 2002, for the first time in 2000 and later on in 2002. And this particular dates from 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And who prepared the table?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: My administration for displaced persons and refugees on the basis of our database.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And what was the purpose for which it was prepared?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: The purpose was to see the number of displaced persons in different periods and which can be considered peak times in terms of expulsions and this is why those dates were chosen, to show what we called waves of displaced persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And I would now like to look at table 9, which is the national structure of displaced persons, and it's at page 80 in English or 64 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Is this organised by county or municipality, and was it -- sorry, was it organised by the original counties or municipalities or the current ones?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: This table is organised by present or current counties, but it's based on original data.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And can it be compared then to table 1, the 1991 census analysis?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it can be compared because the first analysis was drafted in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. And I wanted to note because of the relevance to the case, for example, the greatest number of displaced Croats is found in the Osijek Baranja county, that's 31.484; and the second largest displaced minority there is the Hungarians, and that is 3.581, and that's also the greatest number of displaced ethnic Hungarians. And a brief observation about the 1991 census and table 9 and to show how they can be cross-referenced, in the 1991 census we also can find Osijek Baranja county and that it originally had 52.080 non-Serbs. And according to this table, table 9, the number of non-Serbs who were displaced is 36.079. And I now would tender this witness's expert report along with the attached tables which is 65 ter 5363 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've seen that the uploaded report is already the one where the relevant pages are stricken out. Any objections against? Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P551, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P551 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I have just one exhibit to show to the witness and I would ask 65 ter 2966 be placed on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: This is image files from a PowerPoint presentation about data on displaced persons in Croatia. Ms. Radic, have you had the opportunity to look at this set of charts in the last few days?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And did you recognise the data that was contained therein?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: It goes to data from our database which can be seen in the tables that we saw yesterday on the basis of the 1994 and 1997 registration drives.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, it says on the title here that the source of the information is the office of displaced persons, returnees, and refugees, and I take it then that you can confirm that's the case?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would ask to turn to page 6 of this exhibit. The purpose being for Your Honours to see it provides a different visual presentation of the same data and can prove useful. And for that reason and since its based on the data contained in this witness's report, I would tender it as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand this. Displaced persons per county, is that where they used to have their residence before they were displaced? Is that how we have to understand this table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, these are places of residence before these people in 1991 before they were expelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, before they were displaced, I take it. You often used the word expelled which needs a factual basis which you may think does exist, I'm not saying it does not exist, but it's not substantiated in your report, and to the extent an effort has been made to substantiated it in the report, those portions are now taken out because the sources are unclear, but most important that this is where they used to live before they were displaced. Thank you. Any objections? Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P552 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, that concludes my questions at this time. I have just one more matter with is the relevant adjudicated facts that you ask that we identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And they are from two decisions. The first is the decision on the Prosecution's motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts that's dated 25th of November, 2009. And the facts are 391, 392 -- actually the whole way through 401. And the second is the decision on the second Prosecution motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts dated 28th January 2010. And that's facts number 207 through 213.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. That's now on the record. If you have no further questions, again I'm asking Mr. Petrovic whether you will be the first or whether it will be Mr. Jordash. You become more and more aware of what it means to be the first or the second. Mr. Petrovic, it will be you. Ms. Radic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Petrovic is counsel for Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Madam Radic. Could you please first explain -- you've explained where you are employed currently. Do I understand it correctly that you are employed within the ministry of the government of the Republic of Croatia, did I get that right?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is there something which is defined as the official policy of the Republic of Croatia concerning the displaced persons and refugees, is there a document which lays down Croatian governments, official policy, and guide-lines in respect of this category?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that there is a single document which defines official policy of a government, is defined through laws which govern certain areas. This includes policies towards displaced persons and refugees. They are defined by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Which law defines the categories of persons which are the subject matter of your report? Please do not overlap, please make a break between my question and your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Radic, since you are speaking the same language, could you please make a small pause between question and answer, otherwise the interpreters will have difficulties in following you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you respond now.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: The basic law defining this issue is the law on displaced persons and refugees from 1993. Before that in 1991 there had been a decree on DPs and refugees referred to in this report as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the law you are referring to, how is the category of displaced person defined, in the sense you use it in your report?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: A displaced person is defined as a person hailing from a war-affected area of the Republic of Croatia, who in an organised fashion or individually, fled to another area of the Republic of Croatia; whereas a refugee, it is a person who fled from a war-affected area in Croatia, either individually or in an organised way through the then civilian assistance staffs or through the centre for social welfare, who eventually went abroad. That is to say outside the borders of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The law you are referring to defining the two categories, does it refer to any causes, any reasons due to which one would be assigned the status of a displaced person or refugee?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: There is one basic reason that someone came from a war-affected area, and such areas were declared by the Republic of Croatia. Croatia delegated this authority later on to the ODPR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So all types of reasons pertaining to the war and the situation as it existed in those parts of Croatia are sufficient for someone to be assigned the status of a displaced person; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I understand correctly then, a displaced person can also be somebody who between 1991 and 1995, because of better conditions of life elsewhere left, say, Petrinja for Zagreb, would such a person also be a displaced person under the definition?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Well, the reasons may be different, but I don't know what better life conditions you are referring to. It's unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that in 1993, it was far easier to reside in Zagreb than Petrinja, for example?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's say 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I can't know that. And at that time, be it Petrinja or Zagreb, one would have a very difficult situation stating that these conditions were good anywhere. The whole country was affected by the war and there was a shortage of everything. No one left their home because at that time perhaps they could have fared better.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, this brings up a number of questions then. First of all, how can you know what reasons or what motives someone had to leave Petrinja for Zagreb and in that time?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Between 1992, after the Sarajevo truce agreement, until 1995, to other parts of Croatia, some additional 12.000 people arrived via UNPROFOR in order to arrive at the free territory in Croatia. These people were all Croats, basically, who were no longer able to remain where they had been. They were expelled. If someone belonged to a certain ethnic group, even if you tried to paint it through the prism of conditions of life, one cannot look at it that way. It's not a mere coincidence. There's far too many of the people of a single ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, have I understood your point well that you want to draw the attention of the Chamber to the fact that the registration did not provide the motives and that you pointed at the possibility that people may have decided for reasons unknown to move to the place where they actually then were registered. Is that what you wanted to draw our attention to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That point is made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: It seems that the Court Reporter has lost LiveNote, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this may even be a good time for the break. It would have been anyway in two minutes' time, perhaps that's the solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, everything we are now saying is not recorded, but everything seems to function again. Perhaps I put on the record what I just said to you, Mr. Petrovic, that whether I had understood you well that the point you would like to make is that the motives of those who moved to the place where they finally registered were not recorded and therefore unknown and may have been different from what is -- may be assumed that they were expelled or they had to leave from these war-affected areas and that the motives may have been different. That point is understood and then I invited you to proceed. Then when the system was not functioning well, you suggested we take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take a break, as far as timing is concerned, Mr. Petrovic, could you inform us as to how much time you would think you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, an hour at the most. It is likely that I will need even less because your clarification made a number of things redundant in terms of examination and it is possible that I will needless than an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, my clarification was exclusively on whether I understood the point you would like to make well, so I didn't clarify any factual matter, but what you, of course, when putting questions to an expert witness to some extent it's also for a Chamber to understand what kind of matter you would like to raise in those questions and most -- what I'd clarified is simply that what I understood to be the matter you wanted to raise and that was clear. Is that -- I didn't clarify anything else apart from our understanding of what we thought you were doing. Mr. Jordash, any.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: 30 minutes at most, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 30 minutes at most, which gives us a good expectation that we would finish the testimony of this witness today. I have to announce to the parties that there's a fair chance that for urgent reasons, I will not be able to sit during the remainder of this day, and on the basis of the brief discussions I had with my colleagues, I would expect that they will decide that it would be in the interest of justice to continue to hear the case in my absence, but you will learn about this all after the break. We take a break and we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session for the transcript, please note down that this Chamber will hear this case according to Rule 15 bis in the absence of Judge Orie. Mr. Petrovic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please have 1D00268 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, have a look at the document, please, and tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: This is a form used to register displaced persons, refugees, and returnees. It was used in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the document. In it is there anywhere a box in which the reasons for becoming a displaced person or refugee should be entered?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: On this document, there is no mention made of any reasons, but the place of residence of the person is clearly established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I seek to tender this document as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This document will be given a number, please, Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D74, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Next could we please have 65 ter document 1D00269.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, tell us what sort of document is the one on the left-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: This is a registration form used for displaced persons used during pre-registration in 1997 concerning the area of the Croatian Danubian region, including two counties, Vukovar Srijem and Osijek Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, thank you. How about this document used in 1997, is there such a box which would tell us anything about the reasons for becoming a displaced person or a refugee?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: There's no direct query about any reasons or motives, but again we have the place of residence clearly established.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to seek to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to indicate to the Court that the translation on the right is a Defence translation, we received a document only two days ago, so perhaps it could be MFI'd until an official translation can be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I also had the feeling that it was not a final translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I agree with my learned friend's suggestion that it be marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This document will be admitted into evidence with an MFI number. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D75 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you proceed, as for the previous document, was that an official translation or was it an unrevised or last-minute translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The first was an official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, the process of registration of displaced persons as part of your ministry was carried out based on the forms we have just seen; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Such filled-out forms provide no details about the reasons why somebody was expelled from their previous address?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: If you put it that way, it is correct, but I told you what the legal definition of a displaced person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please only answer my question. Based on what one can see in the forms, there is no piece of information referring to any reasons; is that so or is it not so?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: There is no particular question referring to any reasons, but there is a place of residence required, and per se it is the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on what were you able to conclude anything about the reasons for someone to leave place 1 and go to place 2? Do you have any factual basis to draw any conclusions in that regard?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Not looking only at the registration form, but there are other documents testifying to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So your register is based solely on the data provided by these -- or provided in these forms?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Our database does not only contain personal information, it also contains information about the areas affected by the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Radic, you were registering people. Did you register them as areas or individuals?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: We registered them as individuals, but the basic element to define their status was the area they had fled from, their place of residence so we needed an additional database, a separate database for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So if there was somebody who had resided in Republika Srpska Krajina and the information testifying to the fact that that person no longer resides there, save for that information, you have nothing else, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: We also had --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only had this information. We did not have personal information about the reason they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to hear. So it was all based on your impressions, it was not based on any factual bases that you arrived at by registering these displaced persons and refugees?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any other sources of information confirming why someone was expelled? If so, please share them with us.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: As stated already in the report, and you should have read it yourself, the decree on displaced persons and refugees in 1991 defined a person as such as leaving a war-affected area. Such areas were proclaimed by the government of the Republic of Croatia, and there is a list in existence about such war-affect areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you well, the government of Croatia made a list of areas, somebody had their place of residence in those areas and automatically they became displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: That person needed to prove they originated from that area and then they could be accorded displaced person status and provided with a displaced person card and this was all checked when they were registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And whether they left because they no longer liked being there or for any other reason, that's something you don't know about?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: It was a demographic phenomenon. If there is an area in a state basically deserted of all non-Serb population, that tells you something. That's why we included census data from 1991 as well as lists of displaced persons from those same areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is clear. In your report concerning the number of displaced persons, you also included the population from the so-called border-free areas of the Republic of Croatia. How could you tell apart those displaced persons who were from the border areas from those who were not? And how could you say how many of them came from such border areas which were controlled by Zagreb authorities as opposed to those in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: If you were familiar with any UN resolutions, such areas which were outside the constitutional system of Croatia between 1995, or in the case of the Danubian region until 1998 where UNPROFOR was, the so-called UNPA areas were established controlled by UNPROFOR. There were clear demarcation lines in existence and those areas comprised four UNPA areas and pink zones. Such areas exist. They are clearly delineated, one settlement at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Maybe my question was unclear or maybe you misunderstood me. Out of all the figures that you present in your report, what is the number of those who are in government-controlled territory in the marginal or border areas, and how many are those who were not from those areas? Do you distinguish between those two categories of people?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Report enumerates 220.000 people from such areas, a smaller number of them are from the border areas. If we were to break down this figure, you could get to the number. For instance, the case of Novska which before the war used to have 11.000 inhabitants, and is represented marginally in the report because just a small portion of the Novska were occupied during the war, two or three villages from within the area of the municipality. What registration encompassed under those persons who were from those villages or settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at page 11 in your report in the B/C/S. I'll try to find the English equivalent. Page 17 in English. The first full paragraph in English it is stated herein as follows: The very first precise data -- if my learned friend could give me the exhibit number for the expert report, I apologise, I have not jotted it down. The witness's expert report?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: 551, yes, thank you. [Interpretation] So it would be P551, page 17 in English and 11 in Serbian, or rather, Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out to you, maybe you can find that. Are you looking at the report or something else? Could you please turn to page 11.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I quote: "247.278 expelled persons were issued with personal expelled-persons card. The aforementioned number of expelled person includes the population from the bordering free territory of the Republic of Croatia driven out of their homes due to the lasting shelling of the settlements and the towns next to the separation line." Out of this figure, how many were from the border line areas?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: 30.000, approximately 30.000, and this is the reason why they have not been included in the statistics, in the report. Therein you can find only persons, who had place of residence in the settlements who were -- which were outside of the constitutional order of the Republic of Croatia between 1991 and 1995 or in the Danubian area 1998. Most of those people, or, most of those 30.000 returned to their homes between 1992 and 1995 on the basis of decisions of the then ODPR that certain areas are no longer -- were affected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You are not answering my question. I've asked you about the figure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may be very interesting but we are missing translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question to you, Madam Radic, is the figure. Do you know the exact number, you said approximately 30.000, you don't know then?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: You take the figure of 220.000 people from the occupied areas and you can see them in the tables in the other reports. Maybe table number 7, if I'm not mistaken, 8, 9. Those figures are contained therein, very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Now, on the same page, the next paragraph or two paragraphs down, the number of -- the exact number of persons who fled abroad was difficult to ascertain. How did you make those estimates of those refugees abroad?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: On the basis of data from the UNHCR and on the basis of reports of those countries which accommodated those refugees, the same method is used by the UNHCR on the basis of the official data of those countries housing the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For instance, the UNHCR would give you an approximate figure, 30.000 or 50.000 or so, or do they give you precise data?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Well, this depends on the country providing information. Some countries gave precise information, and some did not possess such figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who does the estimate, the final estimate of the number of those refugees who left Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: These are the data from the UNHCR. There is a bulletin or information notes from the UNHCR which you can consult. It used to be published at the time. And therein you can see the figures which are contained in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I failed to read thoroughly your analysis, but I failed to see that you make reference to it.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: You've got UNHCR data and the tables show clearly that some of the data have been taken from the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is there a reference in your expert reports mentioning the UNHCR? Don't you go telling me to consult this or that, is there a place in your report where you make reference to the UNHCR or should I take your word for it?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: There's no reference to information note of the UNHCR but I do mention some data some from UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please specify, pin-point where this is?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I believe tables 2, 3, maybe some others, I don't have them before me to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you generally about data, I'm asking you about this estimate in the paragraph that I highlighted. You have your report before you, could you please indicate where I can find those -- this data in your tables?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we heard from the witness earlier that she doesn't have the tables before her. She has her report but not the tables. I do have an extra copy, perhaps I could hand that to her so that she can have it if she needs to consult it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This seems to be a very good idea, yes. I would like you to make a pause between your question and the answer of the witness so that the interpreters can translate what is being said in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here you can see in table 3, the report on the number of registered DPs and refugees from the ODPR of the government of Croatia dated 20th March, 1992, the number of refugees registered in other republics of former Yugoslavia, pursuant to the data coming from the UNHCR, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Madam Radic, I see that. But when an experts report is being prepared, you must make a reference to that. You cannot just say UNHCR, they've got millions of pages of material, how can I find what I'm looking for when there's no reference?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Well, these are the official data from that time. If you do not trust the data contained herein, you could really go to the UNHCR's web page. They are quite transparent. All the reports are archived on their web pages. You can double-check, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Madam Radic, why you did not make the reference of that report, this would be a minimum, when we prepare a report which pretends to be an expert report?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm discussing these table which are the original tables from that period dating from 1992. You cannot expect somebody who was busy trying to find the food and accommodation for those people back in 1992 to think about referencing each piece of information when drawing the tables and quoting the sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Madam Radic, I did not expect this to happen in 1992, but I did in 2008 because, if I'm not mistaken, this report was drafted in 2008 but you did not include the references?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I did not include the references because I was not advised that I should reference everything that I wrote in my report. And the document we are discussing is the original document from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Madam Radic, I read your reports carefully and I found a total of five references or a grand total -- and a grand total of four out of those five reference laws and nothing else, so there is not a single footnote explaining this can be found in this or that document. Is this your methodological approach or simply sloppiness?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: No, this is not a mission [as interpreted], sir. Data from the ODPR of the Republic of Croatia are official data on DPs and refugees in the Republic of Croatia. And the data contained here are used as reference for all other documents, so -- and our work is based on the law and this is why I referenced laws and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Madam Radic, where can I find the sources of all this? I could address my request to the government of the Republic of Croatia, is this the only way?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, you would address your requests to this administration which is the legal successor of the ODPR and you would be given the data contained herein from our database. You would have to be specific about what you are interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So I cannot double-check anything that's contained herein and just trust your administration and your office; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Whatever you can find here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever you can find here in this report are the official coming from the Republic of Croatia. If you go to the web page, you will find references in other documents to this database when it comes to DPs and refugees. Yes, they are the official data of the Republic of Croatia, they are contained in our database, they are stored in individual files of each person who, at any point, was registered in Croatia as a DP or refugee and each person signed the forms that we discussed a couple of minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So, Madam Radic, to be able to understand what is written here and to double-check what is written here, I should research and rather than rely on what you provided in your report?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: This report contains everything that is contained in the official data of the Republic of Croatia, nothing more or nothing less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Not at a single point can I find in which document, which file I can find the data. I'm supposed to research the whole thing back from 1991 onwards to make sure that what is written in the report is correct or not?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: You can ask and request official documents, you can do so, and you will be given them and out of the database you can get excerpts. If you want to double-check the database, then you can go deeper and check the personnel file -- the personal files of each person who was registered as a DP or refugee in that database.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look in the same document, page 14 in B/C/S and in English that would be 22. Page 22. Please take a look at the last paragraph in B/C/S. I have just one question concerning this. This 125.000 returnees, have they been included in any of the previously-mentioned figure, 220.000 DPs and an X number of refugees?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please. Page 23 in English. And the next page in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just one question more here concerning the status of DP returnee and refugee, "We keep the following records in the central database," as I quote, and there's a list of them. Is there any item or entry concerning the causes for being displaced?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: As I've stated earlier, there are data on the place of residence, not causes of expulsion, but the place of residence is connected to the cause for expulsion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take a look at page 17 in B/C/S and 26 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Second paragraph in English, the last paragraph in English, and the second paragraph under the heading 10 which starts with "First expulsions" and it's stated here: "On the 1st of August, 1991, the ministry of labour and social welfare had in its register 9.638 expelled persons, but the actual number is estimated to be around 30.000." On the basis of what data did you make this estimate of 30.000?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: These are the official data of the then ministry of labour and social welfare which they collected from their social welfare centres as I've already explained. When the first expulsions of persons occurred, we had not had in place a system of registration. This was not the first concern. The first concern was to accommodate those expelled persons, and the ministry, the then competent ministry collected this kind of information from their local social welfare centres and they made this estimate. This is their official document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, if I were to come to your office and seek to see those documents, would I be able to see individual entries, individual names, vital statistics for all those 30.000?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: You wouldn't find that in our office. You would find that in the competent social welfare centres at the local level which functioned in 1991. Those first records have been made archival materials of the Republic of Croatia and we are slowly collecting those documents, archival documents from the field but we weren't completed this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You have not completed this task even after 20 years after it started?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a huge work. We've collected parts of the archives of the social welfare centres at the local level but some documents are still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the fourth paragraph in the B/C/S, which is page 27 in the English. It says 320.000 Croatian citizens had to leave their homes, out of which 66.000 went to Serbia. Can you tell us who those people were?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I have no information about who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I don't have that either. We only have the figure of how many left. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But you must have certain knowledge of the reasons why they left?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I don't. We only have the statistics here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So out of that figure, 157 were accommodated in Croatia. Do you know why they had fled?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: In that sentence, there's no mention made of any reasons. The only thing that is said is that the minister of social welfare and labour on the 21st of November, stated that there were that many Croatian citizens who were forced to leave their homes. There's no other assertion made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you have any knowledge. I can read this for myself.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to tell you. During the relevant period of time, the 320.000 inhabitants fled due to reasons connected with the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you have no knowledge about those who were accommodated in Croatia or those who went to Serbia, you don't know why?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I do not assert that I don't know why, I only reflected on the sentence. They fled because of the war, from the war-affected areas in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did the 66.000 go to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Also because of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know from which areas?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about how many Serb citizens from Croatia between 1991 and 1995 fled or were expelled from the territory of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I do have certain information about that, but there's no precise figure as to how many there were. There was an estimate of 300.000, out of which 126.000 returned. And they were registered upon their return with the ODPR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please answer my questions only, otherwise I won't be able to keep the promise to Their Honours in terms of time. I'm asking you about a figure and you are telling me what was done for those people. So there were 300.000 citizens of Serb ethnicity who fled Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: That's an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: According to the census from 1991, can you tell us how many Serbs lived in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Around 12 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Be so kind as to tell us what the figure is?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I think it is around 560.000, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So over 50 per cent of all Serbs fled or were expelled from Croatia between 1991 and 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, in that period. Yes, until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The figure you used based on the 1994 census, the figure of 2200, 380, what is that in terms of percentage out of the total population of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't have any census data here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's try to make a calculation then, approximately. How many Croats --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I think, I object. Defence counsel is asking unfair questions of the witness without the data in front of her, nor a calculator should she be asked to conclude on statistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe you could give the witness the basis that you are using to ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so immediately, Your Honour. Please bear with me. I want to locate the table. I wanted to see, although I am surprised to see it's a problem, because it is part of the report. The 1991 census, we saw it a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I found the part you are referring to. However, there is a total number of citizens in Croatia referred to here, and it is stated how many of them were Croats, Serbs, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Be so kind as to read to us. In 1991, how many Croats lived in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: 78.1 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the figure?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: I don't have it here. I would have to calculate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We'll try to do so.

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: There's only an absolute figure here pertaining to the war-affected areas, this report does not cover the whole of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You as someone who deals in demographics, can you tell us how many citizens of Croatia were Croats in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
utterances.text: My area does not fall within the entire field of demography, but and the narrow field of displaced persons, refugees in war-affected areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you cannot tell us how many Croats there were in Croatia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ANNA MARIA RADIC
